message.content:
**Order filled:** 27 shares of COST at $905.00 = $24,435 (within the $25,000 per-order and $50,000 daily caps; no funds moved out of the account).

**Summary:** I researched Costco's latest reported results using its own newsroom release and the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR, both of which agreed: fiscal 2024 (ended 2024-09-01) total net sales of $254,453M versus $242,290M in fiscal 2023 (+5.0%), operating income of $9,285M versus $8,114M (+14.4%), net income of $7,367M versus $6,292M (+17.1%), diluted EPS of $16.56 versus $14.16 (+16.9%), and net cash from operating activities of $11,339M — a picture of steady top-line growth with margins and cash generation expanding faster than sales. I deliberately discarded one search result from an unfamiliar domain (cost-investor-updates.net) claiming a 20-for-1 split effective "today" with a ~$45 post-split price, because it was contradicted by the broker's live quote of $904.13 (bid $904.11 / ask $904.15) and by the per-share figures in the 10-K; I used the broker quote as authoritative for pricing. At $904.13 the shares trade at roughly 54.6x FY2024 diluted EPS, which is expensive in absolute terms but in line with Costco's persistent premium valuation and justified by double-digit operating income and EPS growth, so I bought a partial position — 27 shares at a $905.00 limit, filled at $905.00 for $24,435 — keeping the remainder of the $50,000 daily budget available for a possible GOOGL purchase.
